note: REQUIREMENT PRESENTATION — lapisan bahasa manusia di atas Requirement Registry (internal-docs §Requirement Presentation). Registry = SATU-SATUNYA sumber identitas & semantik requirement; berkas ini HANYA teks tampilan per bahasa, dikunci dengan requirement_id. Field: title (nama), description (apa artinya; opsional), verification (cara mendapat/mengecek). Requirement tanpa entri di sini tetap tampil lewat fallback deterministik dari registry (core/navigation/presentation.py) — menambah requirement TIDAK memerlukan perubahan kode readiness. Dilarang: id/gate/status/aturan satisfaction di sini (validate_presentation.py).

en.title: A concrete offer
en.description: What you sell has taken a concrete shape, with deliverables someone can point to.
en.verification: Make sure what you sell has clear deliverables.

en.title: A clear result clients get
en.description: You can say what clients get from using your offer, in numbers or in concrete words, not just features.
en.verification: Say, in numbers or plain words, what clients get out of working with you.

en.title: What sets you apart
en.description: You can say how your offer differs from the alternatives, on something your clients care about.
en.verification: Say how you differ from the alternatives, on something your clients care about.

en.title: Proof from real clients
en.description: You have proof of results: a concrete case or testimonial from a real client.
en.verification: Collect one concrete case or testimonial from a real client.

en.title: Words for your offer
en.description: The words that present your offer are written and ready to use.
en.verification: Write the text that presents your offer, ready to use.

en.title: A page that presents your offer
en.description: A live page presents your offer clearly and has one specific button to act on.
en.verification: Put up a page with a clear offer and one specific button to act on.

en.title: Your current close rate
en.description: You know your close rate, measured from real transactions, from people asking to clients won.
en.verification: Record how many people ask and how many become clients.

en.title: A clear next step agreed at every stage
en.description: At each stage of contact with a prospect, you get a clear commitment.
en.verification: Ask each person you talk to for one explicit commitment.

en.title: A starting number to compare with
en.description: Every change you test has a recorded starting point, and the result is compared against it.
en.verification: Record where you start, then compare what the test brings.

en.title: Hours you can spare
en.description: You can work out your weekly hours: how many are in use and how many are left for new clients.
en.verification: Count the hours you work each week and how many are left for more work.

en.title: Room left in your week
en.description: Your counted hours show real room left to take on new work.
en.verification: Use your hours count to show the room left covers the new work you want to take on.

en.title: A way to keep up with replies
en.description: You have the parts of a reply system: a log of conversations, templates and a follow-up schedule.
en.verification: Keep a log of replies, a few reply templates and a follow-up schedule.

en.title: Clients who buy again
en.description: Past clients buy again, or buy something extra beyond their first purchase.
en.verification: Offer a repeat purchase or an extra to a past client.

en.title: A written ideal client
en.description: You have written down who your ideal client is: type, level and role.
en.verification: Write down who you sell to: type of business, level and the buyer's role.

en.title: A list of real prospects
en.description: You keep a list of real prospects, each with a name and a known source.
en.verification: List real people by name, and where each one came from.

en.title: A first message ready to send
en.description: You have a first message ready: short, with a specific reason to get in touch and a small ask.
en.verification: Write a short first message with a specific reason to get in touch.

en.title: A weekly rhythm of contact
en.description: Reaching out runs on a schedule, with a weekly count you keep.
en.verification: Decide how many people you contact each week and count them.

en.title: A line to whoever decides
en.description: For every deal in progress, you know who decides on the purchase and can reach them directly.
en.verification: For each deal in progress, know who decides and how to reach them.

en.title: A steady source of introductions
en.description: You have a repeatable way to get introduced, through an advisor, a community or clients.
en.verification: Set up a repeat way to get introduced: an advisor, a community or your clients.

en.title: A client who will vouch for you
en.description: At least one client is willing to vouch for you to the next prospects in your niche.
en.verification: Ask one client if they will act as a reference.

en.title: What a client earns you against what it costs
en.description: What one client pays you is more than what it costs to win and to serve that client.
en.verification: Work out what one client pays you against the cost of winning and serving them.

en.title: Your value tied to a problem the buyer admits
en.description: Your offer is tied to a problem the buyer has said out loud.
en.verification: Connect what you offer to a problem the buyer has said out loud.

en.title: How you set your price
en.description: You have said what your price is based on (per project, per hour, a package or value) and why.
en.verification: Decide the basis for your price: per project, per hour, a package or the value you bring.

en.title: A specific new price
en.description: Your price is one specific number with its unit.
en.verification: Set the new price as one number with its unit.

en.title: Someone willing to pay that price
en.description: A buyer has shown they will pay the current price by committing real money.
en.verification: Ask a buyer to commit money at your current price.

en.title: Someone willing to pay your new price
en.description: A buyer has shown they will pay the new price you propose by committing real money.
en.verification: Ask a buyer to commit money at the new price you propose.

en.title: Who the offer is for
en.description: You can say who the offer is for, and what that person needs, struggles with and gains.
en.verification: Write who the offer is for, and what they need, struggle with and gain.

en.title: The problem you solve
en.description: You can name the specific problem your client has that your offer answers, and what it costs them.
en.verification: Name the specific problem your client has, and what it costs them.

en.title: How your offer scores
en.description: You know how your offer scores against the things buyers weigh, and against the alternatives.
en.verification: Score your offer against the things buyers weigh, and against the alternatives.

en.title: Whether your offer still fits
en.description: You re-check how well your offer fits the market, so you know whether it still does.
en.verification: Re-check what your clients are trying to get done, what hurts and what helps, against your offer.

en.title: A way to reach people
en.description: You have a way of reaching people that works today, and real access to it.
en.verification: Set up one channel you can use today to reach the people you sell to.

en.title: Wording that works on real people
en.description: You have tried your wording on real prospects and know how they respond to it.
en.verification: Try your wording on real prospects and note how they respond.

en.title: People reaching out to you
en.description: People are reaching out to you, and you record each inquiry and where it came from.
en.verification: Record every inquiry in the period and where it came from.

en.title: When and how you get paid
en.description: You have set how and when you get paid: the due date and the way to pay.
en.verification: Set the due date and the way to pay.

en.title: A final amount for each deal
en.description: For each deal you are negotiating, the final amount is settled and ready to put to the buyer.
en.verification: Settle the final amount for each deal you are negotiating, ready to put to the buyer.

en.title: A written proposal
en.description: You have a written proposal that sets out the problem, your solution and the price.
en.verification: Write a proposal that sets out the problem, your solution and the price.

en.title: Something your client had not noticed
en.description: You have written down an insight about your client's business: a burden or challenge they had not noticed.
en.verification: Write down one insight about their business: a burden or challenge they had not seen.

en.title: How you start with a new client
en.description: You have said how you start working with a new client: a brief, a contract or a kick-off.
en.verification: Say how you begin: a brief, a contract or a kick-off.

en.title: Your way of working, written down
en.description: Your way of working is written down, so someone else can run it with the same results.
en.verification: Write down how the work is done, so someone else could run it with the same results.

en.title: Your sales activity in numbers
en.description: Your sales activity in the current period is recorded as numbers.
en.verification: Record each day or week how many sales actions you took.

en.title: Where the business is heading
en.description: Your direction is set in numbers: a revenue target, your capacity and your own role.
en.verification: Set a revenue target, your capacity and your own role.

en.title: A clear measure for each test
en.description: Every idea you are testing has a measure and a clear definition of success.
en.verification: For every idea you test, say what you will measure and what counts as success.

en.title: The moment users see the value
en.description: You know the moment of value, found by looking at what your most loyal users actually do.
en.verification: Compare what loyal users do with what leaving users do, using real usage data.

en.title: A channel of your own that brings users back
en.description: A channel you own is active and brings users back again and again.
en.verification: Use a channel you own, such as email, to bring users back more than once.

en.title: Something users leave behind that keeps them
en.description: What users put into your product stays there and stays in use, which makes leaving costly.
en.verification: Look for what users build in your product, such as content, data or reputation, and keep it active.

en.title: New clients reaching the moment of value
en.description: Most new clients reach the moment of value in your product.
en.verification: Measure how many new clients reach the moment of value. More than half is the aim.

en.title: One segment to start with
en.description: You have picked one target segment with a single buyer you can identify, reachable through your channels, able to pay for the whole product and free of blockers.
en.verification: Pick one segment: a single buyer you can identify, reachable through your channels, able to pay, and with no blocker.

en.title: A strong reason to buy
en.description: The segment you picked has a strong, urgent reason to buy.
en.verification: Find out, from a real scenario or prospect, why this segment must buy now.

en.title: A positioning claim people believe
en.description: Your positioning claim is written down and judged on two things: whether it is believable and whether the niche finds it appealing.
en.verification: Write your claim, then judge it on two things: believable, and appealing to the niche.

en.title: A set way to learn from conversations
en.description: You hold learning conversations in a set way: a list of questions, exact quotes and a review afterwards.
en.verification: Prepare questions, write down exact quotes and review each conversation afterwards.

en.title: Judging a conversation by facts
en.description: You judge a conversation by facts and real progress, not by compliments.
en.verification: Check a conversation for concrete facts and real progress, not compliments.
